deliverables_scope.text: ===== FILE: files/ATTACHMENT_1_SOW_1232SA26Q1231.pdf ===== Statement of Work (SOW) USDA / Twist Bioscience / HudsonAlpha Sorghum Genomics Project — Community-Driven Target Design and High-Throughput Genotyping via Custom Hybrid Capture Participating Organizations: ● USDA (Doreen Ware Lab): Community coordination, target specification, and sample provision. ● Twist Bioscience: Probe design, printing, validation, and provision of FlexPrep Ultra- High-Throughput Library Prep Kits at a reduced cost. ● HudsonAlpha Institute for Biotechnology: Experimental execution including calibration of all plant-specific protocols for Sorghum seeds and optimization of sequencing methods. 1. Project Overview This collabor

Project Overview This collaborative project combines community coordination by USDA, probe manufacturing by Twist Bioscience, and HudsonAlpha’s Sorghum-optimized sequencing and analysis workflows. It will deliver high-quality genotype data supporting genetic diversity and breeding objectives. 2. Scope of Work Khufu – Hybrid capture genotyping 120 quantity - per 96-well plate. Project Overview This collaborative project combines community coordination by USDA, probe manufacturing by Twist Bioscience, and HudsonAlpha’s Sorghum-optimized sequencing and analysis workflows. It will deliver high-quality genotype data supporting genetic diversity and breeding objectives. 2. Scope of Work Khufu – Hybrid capture genotyping 120 quantity - per 96-well plate. Includes DNA extraction, Library prep, enrichment pooling, Sequencing and variant calling at the sample volume and panel size indicated in the quote header. Deliverables are genotype calls and imputation in hapmap format Twist flex prep and enrichment panel 120 quantity- flex prep kits and panel design and printing for the sample volume and panel size indicated at the quote header 2.1 Community-Driven Probe Design (USDA and Twist Bioscience) ● USDA collects community input to define target genes, variants, and loci of interest. ● Twist Bioscience designs, refines, and validates the hybrid-capture probe panel to match these specifications. ● HudsonAlpha receives the validated panel and optimizes capture conditions for the Sorghum genome. 2.2 DNA Extraction (HudsonAlpha) ● HudsonAlpha extracts DNA from Sorghum seeds using calibrated, plant-optimized methods developed to overcome high polysaccharide and polyphenolic content. references_experience.text: Location The village of Eek is located on the south bank of the Eek River, approximately 35 miles south of Bethel, Alaska. The site is located in the northeast ¼ of the southwest ¼ of Section 31, Township 2 North, Range 73 West, Seward Meridian, Alaska (Baird Inlet A-1 USGS Quadrangle). The Vicinity Map is included as Figure 1 (Appendix A). The legal address of the former BIA property is Lots 1, 2, and 3, US Survey 2021. The property boundaries are shown on Figure 2 in Appendix A. 1.3 Background The following documents were reviewed for history on the environmental activities previously conducted at the site. The sample locations referenced below are shown on Figure 2 (Appendix A). Site Characterization Report – FINAL Eek Old BIA School and Tanks; ADEC File No. 2412.38.004 May 2026 2 SLR. Final Property Assessment and Cleanup Plan, Old BIA School Property, Eek, Alaska. February 2011. A Property Assessment and Cleanup Plan (PACP) was prepared for the old BIA school property site for the purpose of the PACP was to provide information to the community for the purpose of acquiring funding for the cleanup and reuse of the property. The Old BIA School Tank Farm contained five 10,000- gallon vertical tanks. Aerial photographs suggest that barrels were used for fuel stor

eded cleanup levels, but soil samples and f ield indications (odor, sheen) suggested that the concentrations may be biogenic in nature. Additional investigation was recommended to determine if contamination extends off property and/or is comingled, determine vertical extent of contamination, collect additional groundwater samples, and determine the depth of permafrost. The 2024 sample locations are included as Figures 2 and 3. 1.4 Property Records A Limited Liability Report was received by First American Title. The following documents were obtained for Lot 3, U.S. Survey No. 2021, Bethel Recording District and copies of the documents referenced above are provided in Appendix B. • Quitclaim Deed recorded March 16, 1989: The BIA granted the property known as the former Eek School Reserve to the State of Alaska Department of Education. • U.S. Survey No. 2021 recorded April 23, 1993: The property was surveyed in August 1991. At the time of the survey, there was a fenced tank farm with five tanks, two houses, a frame building, three sheds, a wood platform and a pumphouse. The size of Lot 3 is 3.06 acres. According to the BIA, Lots 1 and 2 were conveyed to the Village of Eek. Documents for these lots were not provided by First American Title. 2.0 CONTAMINANTS OF CONCERN AND APPL

Smoking is prohibited inside any buildings at the VAMC. Possession of weapons is prohibited. Enclosed containers, including tool kits, shall be subject to search. Violations of VA regulations may result in citation answerable in the United States (Federal) District Court, not a local district, state, or municipal court Security Requirements All contractor personnel shall obtain a short-term identification badge issued by the VA REP or government designated representative. Such badge shall be worn by the individual and prominently displayed at all times while on VA Property. No employee of the contractor shall enter the project site without a valid identification badge issued by the VA. In order to obtain a short-term identification badge, contractor personnel shall present to the VA REP a valid (non-expired) photo identification issued by a US federal, state or local government agency. 16; Standard Test Method for Evaluating Rubber Property – Retraction at Lower Temperatures (TR Test) 2.16. Federal Test Method Standard No. 601; Rubber: Sampling and Testing 3. REQUIREMENTS 3.1. The testing laboratory must be certified/accredited to ISO 17025 by an organization certified/accredited to ISO 17011. 3.1.1. The Scope of Certification/Accreditation for the laboratory shall have all test methods required of this statement of work, as applicable. 4. RESPONSIBILITITES 4.1. The testing laboratory shall provide first article testing to 8 rubber formulations based upon various military performance specifications following the referenced ASTMs and additional testing requirements per specifications. 4.1.1. Portsmouth Naval Shipyard and the contracted laboratory shall discuss sampling requirements so that Portsmouth Naval Shipyard can provide adequate material to perform all testing herein. 4.2. Each formulation shall be fully first article tested once by the testing laboratory. After award, the testing laboratory and Portsmouth Naval Shipyard shall discuss what and how many different types of samples the testing laboratory will need. 4.3. The contract shall contain options that include fully testing each additional formula 2 more times, if necessary. This is to allo

Crucially, this support must include Defective Media Retention (DMR) to allow the government to retain failed high-capacity flash storage media upon replacement. This is a mandatory requirement to comply with DoD and Army data se

ates, and onsite repair capabilities for existing HPE Nimble storage hardware. DODI 8500.2 requires supported hardware and software. Maintaining active OEM support ensures high availability and data integrity for the enterprise storage environment and maintains compliance with cybersecurity mandates.
